record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: With the same notation as in Question 5.1, is there a Borel map G from Auth^{<∞}(I, λ) into the disjoint union over n of Diff(T^n, λ^n) such that each system (I, λ, T) is Kakutani equivalent to (T^n, λ^n, G(T))?

evidence.quote: Let (I, λ) be the interval Lebesgue space and (Πn, λn) the n-torus Lebesgue space. We have that Auth<∞(I, λ) is the space of (Lebesgue) measure-preserving automorphisms of I with finite entropy and Diff(Πn, λn) the space of (Lebesgue) measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of Πn.
Question 5.2 (Rodriguez Hertz). Is there a Borel map G : Auth<∞(I, λ) → ⋃n Diff(Πn, λn), such that (I, λ, T ) is Kakutani equivalent to (Πn, λn, G(T )).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(I,\lambda)$ denote the unit interval with Lebesgue measure, and for each positive integer $n$ let $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus with normalized Lebesgue measure. Let $\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$ be the Polish space of invertible Lebesgue measure-preserving automorphisms of $(I,\lambda)$ with finite Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, endowed with the weak topology, and for each $n$ let $\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^n$ preserving $\lambda^n$. Two measure-preserving systems $(X,\mu,S)$ and $(Y,\nu,R)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if they have measurably isomorphic induced systems on positive-measure subsets, equivalently if each is isomorphic to a measurable time-change (suspension/induced map) of the other.

Question: Does there exist a Borel map
$$G:\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)\longrightarrow \bigsqcup_{n\geq 1}\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$$
such that for every $T\in\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$, the system $(I,\lambda,T)$ is Kakutani equivalent to $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n,G(T))$, where $n=n(T)$ is the dimension of the torus into which $T$ is mapped?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent anti-classification results (Foreman–Gerber–Kunde and collaborators) show that Kakutani equivalence among smooth diffeomorphisms of tori is highly non-classifiable, which makes a uniform Borel smooth realization map of this type appear difficult; no published Borel selection of this kind is known, and the question is posed as an open problem attributed to Rodriguez Hertz. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for the Kakutani equivalence relation
status_evidence.snippet: Anti-classification results for ergodic area-preserving smooth diffeomorphisms of the disk, annulus, and 2-torus, as well as real-analytic diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus.
status_evidence.claim: Kakutani equivalence on smooth diffeomorphisms is shown to be non-classifiable, indicating that Borel uniformizations of Kakutani equivalence by smooth systems are subtle and not established.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for weakly mixing diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Anti-classification results for weakly mixing diffeomorphisms of tori.
status_evidence.claim: Related anti-classification results constrain but do not resolve the existence of a Borel Kakutani-realization map into diffeomorphism groups of tori.
